=== markitai -h (exit 0, stderr 0 bytes) ===
Convert documents and URLs to Markdown

Usage: markitai [OPTIONS] [INPUT] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  config  Inspect or edit configuration
  init    Create or update a configuration file with detected API models
  doctor  Diagnose configured workflows and optional native backends
  cache   Inspect or clear the LLM and URL fetch caches
  auth    Inspect subscription authentication or delegate login to an official runtime
  serve   Run the native REST conversion service and web interface
  mcp     Run the native MCP service over standard input/output

Arguments:
  [INPUT]
          Document, URL, .urls list, directory or atomic .numbers package

Options:
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version

Output:
  -o, --output <PATH>
          Output directory, or exact .md path for a single input. Omit for Markdown on stdout
      --json
          Print one JSON result on stdout; requires -o. Usage errors remain on stderr
      --dry-run
          Preview discovery without conversion or output publication
      --record-history
          Archive this run for `markitai serve` history (--no-record-history disables); stdout-only
          conversions are not archived

Configuration:
  -c, --config <PATH>
          Configuration path; must exist except for config set/edit, which can create it
      --config-json <JSON>
          Deep-merge inline JSON over the config file; explicit conversion flags still win
  -p, --preset <NAME>
          Use minimal, standard, rich or a configured preset (case-insensitive)
      --profile <NAME>
          Shape assets/frontmatter for rag, obsidian or okf; independent of the preset [possible
          values: rag, obsidian, okf]
  -I, --interactive
          Choose a conversion in a terminal; edits apply to this session only

LLM, OCR and screenshots:
      --llm
          Enable model processing (--no-llm disables). The last of a flag pair wins; without either,
          the configuration decides
      --alt
          Generate image alt text when LLM processing is enabled (--no-alt disables)
      --desc
          Write image descriptions when LLM processing is enabled (--no-desc disables)
      --ocr
          Read scanned content: macOS Vision locally, or page images with a vision model (--no-ocr
          disables)
      --screenshot
          Capture supported document pages or browser pages; optional backends may be required
          (--no-screenshot disables)
      --screenshot-only
          Use screenshots as content (implies --screenshot). With --llm, read pixels; without --llm,
          ordinary web pages save images without Markdown. PDF media retains Markdown. URL --pure
          takes precedence
      --pure
          Preserve source text without ordinary generated metadata; URL pure takes precedence over
          visual LLM input (--no-pure disables)
      --keep-base
          Keep the base Markdown alongside enhanced output
      --llm-concurrency <N>
          Maximum in-flight model requests shared by this conversion run

URL fetching and backends:
  -s, --strategy <NAME>
          URL strategy: auto (static, then the local browser; remote services only after you opt in
          with fetch.remote_consent), static or playwright run locally; defuddle, jina and
          cloudflare (your account) send the URL to that remote service [possible values: auto,
          static, playwright, defuddle, jina, cloudflare]
  -b, --backend <NAME>
          File backend: native, or cloudflare to convert supported files with Workers AI in your
          Cloudflare account (the file is uploaded) [possible values: native, cloudflare]
      --no-remote-fetch
          Forbid remote extraction services; does not disable explicitly configured model requests

Batch processing:
      --resume
          Resume a directory or .urls batch with matching paths/options; completed entries stay
          completed
  -j, --batch-concurrency <N>
          Maximum concurrent file conversions; independent of URL and model request limits
      --url-concurrency <N>
          Maximum concurrent URL conversions, separately from file processing
  -g, --glob <PATTERN>
          Include/exclude relative directory paths; repeatable, ! prefix excludes. Quote patterns in
          the shell
      --max-depth <N>
          Directory scan depth; 0 scans only the input directory
      --llm-batch
          Submit directory text enhancement to the OpenAI Batch API; --resume continues frozen work
          in -o
      --llm-batch-timeout <SECONDS>
          Maximum local wait for a provider batch (seconds, at least 60); expiry does not cancel it
      --llm-batch-collect <BATCH_ID>
          Collect a saved provider batch into its original -o directory; no input is required

Cache and images:
      --no-cache
          Bypass cache reads while still writing successful fresh results (--cache restores reads)
      --no-cache-for <PATTERNS>
          Comma-separated glob patterns that bypass cache reads for matching inputs
      --no-compress
          Disable image compression (--compress enables it)

Messages and logging:
  -v, --verbose
          Show details such as the report path. Single inputs are otherwise quiet by default: only
          the written path, warnings and errors; stdout Markdown stays clean
  -q, --quiet
          Print errors only: no written path, warnings, progress or batch summary
      --log-level <LEVEL>
          Conversion file-log level; needs log.dir. Console output still follows --verbose/--quiet
          [possible values: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL]

Presets (-p):
  minimal   plain conversion, no model processing
  standard  --llm --alt --desc
  rich      --llm --alt --desc --screenshot

Examples:
  markitai report.docx                     Print Markdown on stdout
  markitai report.pdf -o out/              Write out/report.pdf.md
  markitai notes.html -o out/notes.md      Choose the exact output file
  markitai ./docs -o out/ -g '**/*.pdf'    Convert the PDFs in a directory
  markitai links.urls -o out/ --resume     Continue an interrupted URL list
  markitai https://example.com -o out/     Convert a web page
  markitai scan.png --ocr                  Read the text of an image
  markitai report.pdf -p standard -o out/  Enhance with the configured model
  markitai init                            Create a configuration file
  markitai doctor                          Check models and optional backends

Exit status: 0 success; 1 failure; 2 usage error or provider batch still pending;
10 some batch items failed; 130/143 interrupted.

=== markitai config -h (exit 0, stderr 0 bytes) ===
Inspect or edit configuration

Usage: markitai config [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list      Show the effective configuration; secrets are redacted
  path      Show which configuration file is in use
  validate  Check a configuration file against the schema
  get       Print one value; sections print as JSON
  set       Validate and save one value; invalid values are not written
  edit      Edit settings in a terminal; each value is validated and saved at once

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Configuration:
  -c, --config <PATH>
          Configuration path; must exist except for config set/edit, which can create it
      --config-json <JSON>
          Deep-merge inline JSON over the config file; explicit conversion flags still win

Keys use dot notation, e.g. llm.enabled or llm.model_list[0].model_name. The file in
use is -c, then MARKITAI_CONFIG, then ./markitai.json, then the user config.json.

Examples:
  markitai config list -f table           Show every effective setting
  markitai config get llm.enabled         Read one value
  markitai config set output.dir ./out    Validate and save one value
  markitai config path                    Show which file is in use

=== markitai init -h (exit 0, stderr 0 bytes) ===
Create or update a configuration file with detected API models

Usage: markitai init [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -y, --yes            Do not prompt: create the file, or add newly detected models to an existing
                       one
  -o, --output <PATH>  Write this file, or markitai.json inside this directory
      --local          Write ./markitai.json in the current directory instead of the user
                       configuration
  -h, --help           Print help (see more with '--help')

Configuration:
  -c, --config <PATH>
          Configuration path; must exist except for config set/edit, which can create it
      --config-json <JSON>
          Deep-merge inline JSON over the config file; explicit conversion flags still win

Examples:
  markitai init                Choose the location and how to treat an existing file
  markitai init -y             Create or update the user configuration without prompts
  markitai init --local        Write ./markitai.json for this project
  markitai init -o cfg.json    Write to a custom path
=== markitai init --help (exit 0, stderr 0 bytes) ===
Create or update a configuration file with detected API models.

Detects API models from the environment (MODEL and provider API keys) without
making requests or saving key values. LLM processing stays disabled in the
generated file; enable it per run with --llm or with
`markitai config set llm.enabled true`.

Usage: markitai init [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -y, --yes
          Do not prompt: create the file, or add newly detected models to an existing one

  -o, --output <PATH>
          Write this file, or markitai.json inside this directory

      --local
          Write ./markitai.json in the current directory instead of the user configuration

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Configuration:
  -c, --config <PATH>
          Configuration path; must exist except for config set/edit, which can create it

      --config-json <JSON>
          Deep-merge inline JSON over the config file; explicit conversion flags still win

Examples:
  markitai init                Choose the location and how to treat an existing file
  markitai init -y             Create or update the user configuration without prompts
  markitai init --local        Write ./markitai.json for this project
  markitai init -o cfg.json    Write to a custom path
=== markitai doctor -h (exit 0, stderr 0 bytes) ===
Diagnose configured workflows and optional native backends

Usage: markitai doctor [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json            Print the checks as one JSON object
      --fix             Install the official Chrome headless shell when no working browser is found
      --suggest-extras  Python package extras; not applicable to this native build and rejected
  -h, --help            Print help (see more with '--help')

Configuration:
  -c, --config <PATH>
          Configuration path; must exist except for config set/edit, which can create it
      --config-json <JSON>
          Deep-merge inline JSON over the config file; explicit conversion flags still win

Examples:
  markitai doctor           Human-readable report
  markitai doctor --json    Machine-readable checks
  markitai doctor --fix     Install a browser when no working one is found
=== markitai doctor --help (exit 0, stderr 0 bytes) ===
Diagnose configured workflows and optional native backends.

Missing optional backends are reported but do not fail. The exit status is 1
only when the configuration asks for something this machine cannot deliver:
an active model whose credentials are missing, a configured browser workflow
that cannot launch, an unavailable subscription runtime, or a failed --fix
repair. No model request is sent and no remote page is opened.

Usage: markitai doctor [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json
          Print the checks as one JSON object

      --fix
          Install the official Chrome headless shell when no working browser is found

      --suggest-extras
          Python package extras; not applicable to this native build and rejected

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Configuration:
  -c, --config <PATH>
          Configuration path; must exist except for config set/edit, which can create it

      --config-json <JSON>
          Deep-merge inline JSON over the config file; explicit conversion flags still win

Examples:
  markitai doctor           Human-readable report
  markitai doctor --json    Machine-readable checks
  markitai doctor --fix     Install a browser when no working one is found
=== markitai cache -h (exit 0, stderr 0 bytes) ===
Inspect or clear the LLM and URL fetch caches

Usage: markitai cache [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  stats        Show cache entry counts and disk use
  clear        Clear the LLM and URL fetch caches
  spa-domains  Inspect or clear learned browser-domain routing

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Configuration:
  -c, --config <PATH>
          Configuration path; must exist except for config set/edit, which can create it
      --config-json <JSON>
          Deep-merge inline JSON over the config file; explicit conversion flags still win

Examples:
  markitai cache stats                    Entry counts and disk use
  markitai cache stats -v --limit 10      Recent LLM entries per model
  markitai cache clear -y                 Clear without a confirmation prompt

Inspect subscription authentication or delegate login to an official runtime

Usage: markitai auth [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

  claude   Claude subscription adapter status
  chatgpt  ChatGPT subscription adapter status

          Configuration path; must exist except for config set/edit, which can create it
      --config-json <JSON>

Examples:
  markitai auth                         Status of every subscription runtime
  markitai auth claude status           One runtime (add --json for scripts)
  markitai auth chatgpt login           Sign in through the official runtime

=== markitai serve -h (exit 0, stderr 0 bytes) ===
Run the native REST conversion service and web interface

Usage: markitai serve [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --host <HOST>              Interface to bind. Clients other than this machine need the access
                                 token printed at startup (or MARKITAI_SERVE_TOKEN) [default:
                                 127.0.0.1]
      --port <PORT>              Port to listen on [default: 3600]
      --no-open                  Do not open a browser after startup
      --no-auth                  Do not require the access token from other machines. They can then
                                 upload files and read or delete history; URL conversion and model
                                 settings stay blocked for them
      --allowed-host <HOSTNAME>  Also accept this name in Host/Origin headers (repeatable);
                                 localhost and IP addresses are always accepted
  -h, --help                     Print help

Configuration:
  -c, --config <PATH>
          Configuration path; must exist except for config set/edit, which can create it
      --config-json <JSON>
          Deep-merge inline JSON over the config file; explicit conversion flags still win

Examples:
  markitai serve                          http://127.0.0.1:3600, opens a browser
  markitai serve --port 8080 --no-open    Another port, no browser
  markitai serve --host 0.0.0.0           LAN access with the printed access token
=== markitai serve --help (exit 0, stderr 0 bytes) ===

                                 upload files and read or delete history; URL conversion and model
                                 settings stay blocked for them

=== markitai mcp --help (exit 0, stderr 0 bytes) ===
Run the native MCP service over standard input/output

Tools: convert_document and convert_url convert one document or page,
batch_convert starts a directory or URL-list job and job_status reports on it.
An MCP client starts this command; it answers on stdout and logs on stderr.

Usage: markitai mcp [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Configuration:
  -c, --config <PATH>
          Configuration path; must exist except for config set/edit, which can create it

      --config-json <JSON>
          Deep-merge inline JSON over the config file; explicit conversion flags still win

Examples:
  markitai mcp                          Serve the tools to an MCP client over stdio
  markitai -c cfg.json mcp              Serve with a particular configuration file
=== markitai config list -h (exit 0, stderr 0 bytes) ===
Show the effective configuration; secrets are redacted

Usage: markitai config list [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -f, --format <FORMAT>  Output format [default: json] [possible values: json, yaml, table]
      --show-secrets     Show secret values instead of redacting them (unsafe for shared logs)
  -h, --help             Print help

Configuration:
  -c, --config <PATH>
          Configuration path; must exist except for config set/edit, which can create it
      --config-json <JSON>
          Deep-merge inline JSON over the config file; explicit conversion flags still win

Examples:
  markitai config list               The whole configuration as JSON
  markitai config list -f table      One setting per line
  markitai config list -f yaml       As YAML

=== markitai config path --help (exit 0, stderr 0 bytes) ===
Show which configuration file is in use

Usage: markitai config path [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Configuration:
  -c, --config <PATH>
          Configuration path; must exist except for config set/edit, which can create it
      --config-json <JSON>
          Deep-merge inline JSON over the config file; explicit conversion flags still win

Examples:
  markitai config path               The file in use, or where files are looked for
  markitai -c other.json config path The file chosen with -c

=== markitai (exit 0, stderr 0 bytes) ===
Convert documents and URLs to Markdown

Usage: markitai [OPTIONS] [INPUT] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  config  Inspect or edit configuration
  init    Create or update a configuration file with detected API models
  doctor  Diagnose configured workflows and optional native backends
  cache   Inspect or clear the LLM and URL fetch caches
  auth    Inspect subscription authentication or delegate login to an official runtime
  serve   Run the native REST conversion service and web interface
  mcp     Run the native MCP service over standard input/output

Arguments:
  [INPUT]
          Document, URL, .urls list, directory or atomic .numbers package

Options:
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version

Output:
  -o, --output <PATH>
          Output directory, or exact .md path for a single input. Omit for Markdown on stdout
      --json
          Print one JSON result on stdout; requires -o. Usage errors remain on stderr
      --dry-run
          Preview discovery without conversion or output publication
      --record-history
          Archive this run for `markitai serve` history (--no-record-history disables); stdout-only
          conversions are not archived

Configuration:
  -c, --config <PATH>
          Configuration path; must exist except for config set/edit, which can create it
      --config-json <JSON>
          Deep-merge inline JSON over the config file; explicit conversion flags still win
  -p, --preset <NAME>
          Use minimal, standard, rich or a configured preset (case-insensitive)
      --profile <NAME>
          Shape assets/frontmatter for rag, obsidian or okf; independent of the preset [possible
          values: rag, obsidian, okf]
  -I, --interactive
          Choose a conversion in a terminal; edits apply to this session only

LLM, OCR and screenshots:
      --llm
          Enable model processing (--no-llm disables). The last of a flag pair wins; without either,
          the configuration decides
      --alt
          Generate image alt text when LLM processing is enabled (--no-alt disables)
      --desc
          Write image descriptions when LLM processing is enabled (--no-desc disables)
      --ocr
          Read scanned content: macOS Vision locally, or page images with a vision model (--no-ocr
          disables)
      --screenshot
          Capture supported document pages or browser pages; optional backends may be required
          (--no-screenshot disables)
      --screenshot-only
          Use screenshots as content (implies --screenshot). With --llm, read pixels; without --llm,
          ordinary web pages save images without Markdown. PDF media retains Markdown. URL --pure
          takes precedence
      --pure
          Preserve source text without ordinary generated metadata; URL pure takes precedence over
          visual LLM input (--no-pure disables)
      --keep-base
          Keep the base Markdown alongside enhanced output
      --llm-concurrency <N>
          Maximum in-flight model requests shared by this conversion run

URL fetching and backends:
  -s, --strategy <NAME>
          URL strategy: auto (static, then the local browser; remote services only after you opt in
          with fetch.remote_consent), static or playwright run locally; defuddle, jina and
          cloudflare (your account) send the URL to that remote service [possible values: auto,
          static, playwright, defuddle, jina, cloudflare]
  -b, --backend <NAME>
          File backend: native, or cloudflare to convert supported files with Workers AI in your
          Cloudflare account (the file is uploaded) [possible values: native, cloudflare]
      --no-remote-fetch
          Forbid remote extraction services; does not disable explicitly configured model requests

Batch processing:
      --resume
          Resume a directory or .urls batch with matching paths/options; completed entries stay
          completed
  -j, --batch-concurrency <N>
          Maximum concurrent file conversions; independent of URL and model request limits
      --url-concurrency <N>
          Maximum concurrent URL conversions, separately from file processing
  -g, --glob <PATTERN>
          Include/exclude relative directory paths; repeatable, ! prefix excludes. Quote patterns in
          the shell
      --max-depth <N>
          Directory scan depth; 0 scans only the input directory
      --llm-batch
          Submit directory text enhancement to the OpenAI Batch API; --resume continues frozen work
          in -o
      --llm-batch-timeout <SECONDS>
          Maximum local wait for a provider batch (seconds, at least 60); expiry does not cancel it
      --llm-batch-collect <BATCH_ID>
          Collect a saved provider batch into its original -o directory; no input is required

Cache and images:
      --no-cache
          Bypass cache reads while still writing successful fresh results (--cache restores reads)
      --no-cache-for <PATTERNS>
          Comma-separated glob patterns that bypass cache reads for matching inputs
      --no-compress
          Disable image compression (--compress enables it)

Messages and logging:
  -v, --verbose
          Show details such as the report path. Single inputs are otherwise quiet by default: only
          the written path, warnings and errors; stdout Markdown stays clean
  -q, --quiet
          Print errors only: no written path, warnings, progress or batch summary
      --log-level <LEVEL>
          Conversion file-log level; needs log.dir. Console output still follows --verbose/--quiet
          [possible values: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL]

Presets (-p):
  minimal   plain conversion, no model processing
  standard  --llm --alt --desc
  rich      --llm --alt --desc --screenshot

Examples:
  markitai report.docx                     Print Markdown on stdout
  markitai report.pdf -o out/              Write out/report.pdf.md
  markitai notes.html -o out/notes.md      Choose the exact output file
  markitai ./docs -o out/ -g '**/*.pdf'    Convert the PDFs in a directory
  markitai links.urls -o out/ --resume     Continue an interrupted URL list
  markitai https://example.com -o out/     Convert a web page
  markitai scan.png --ocr                  Read the text of an image
  markitai report.pdf -p standard -o out/  Enhance with the configured model
  markitai init                            Create a configuration file
  markitai doctor                          Check models and optional backends

Exit status: 0 success; 1 failure; 2 usage error or provider batch still pending;
10 some batch items failed; 130/143 interrupted.

--- stderr ---

          (--no-screenshot disables)
      --screenshot-only
          Use screenshots as content (implies --screenshot). With --llm, read pixels; without --llm,
          ordinary web pages save images without Markdown. PDF media retains Markdown. URL --pure
          takes precedence
      --pure
          Preserve source text without ordinary generated metadata; URL pure takes precedence over
          visual LLM input (--no-pure disables)
      --keep-base
          Keep the base Markdown alongside enhanced output
      --llm-concurrency <N>
          Maximum in-flight model requests shared by this conversion run

URL fetching and backends:
  -s, --strategy <NAME>
          URL strategy: auto (static, then the local browser; remote services only after you opt in
          with fetch.remote_consent), static or playwright run locally; defuddle, jina and
          cloudflare (your account) send the URL to that remote service [possible values: auto,
          static, playwright, defuddle, jina, cloudflare]
  -b, --backend <NAME>
          File backend: native, or cloudflare to convert supported files with Workers AI in your
          Cloudflare account (the file is uploaded) [possible values: native, cloudflare]
      --no-remote-fetch
          Forbid remote extraction services; does not disable explicitly configured model requests

Batch processing:
      --resume
          Resume a directory or .urls batch with matching paths/options; completed entries stay
          completed
  -j, --batch-concurrency <N>
          Maximum concurrent file conversions; independent of URL and model request limits
      --url-concurrency <N>
          Maximum concurrent URL conversions, separately from file processing
  -g, --glob <PATTERN>
          Include/exclude relative directory paths; repeatable, ! prefix excludes. Quote patterns in
          the shell
      --max-depth <N>
          Directory scan depth; 0 scans only the input directory
      --llm-batch
          Submit directory text enhancement to the OpenAI Batch API; --resume continues frozen work
          in -o
      --llm-batch-timeout <SECONDS>
          Maximum local wait for a provider batch (seconds, at least 60); expiry does not cancel it
      --llm-batch-collect <BATCH_ID>
          Collect a saved provider batch into its original -o directory; no input is required

Cache and images:
      --no-cache
          Bypass cache reads while still writing successful fresh results (--cache restores reads)
      --no-cache-for <PATTERNS>
          Comma-separated glob patterns that bypass cache reads for matching inputs
      --no-compress
          Disable image compression (--compress enables it)

Messages and logging:
  -v, --verbose
          Show details such as the report path. Single inputs are otherwise quiet by default: only
          the written path, warnings and errors; stdout Markdown stays clean
  -q, --quiet
          Print errors only: no written path, warnings, progress or batch summary
      --log-level <LEVEL>
          Conversion file-log level; needs log.dir. Console output still follows --verbose/--quiet
          [possible values: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL]

Presets (-p):
  minimal   plain conversion, no model processing
  standard  --llm --alt --desc
  rich      --llm --alt --desc --screenshot

Examples:
  markitai report.docx                     Print Markdown on stdout
  markitai report.pdf -o out/              Write out/report.pdf.md
  markitai notes.html -o out/notes.md      Choose the exact output file
  markitai ./docs -o out/ -g '**/*.pdf'    Convert the PDFs in a directory
  markitai links.urls -o out/ --resume     Continue an interrupted URL list
  markitai https://example.com -o out/     Convert a web page
  markitai scan.png --ocr                  Read the text of an image
  markitai report.pdf -p standard -o out/  Enhance with the configured model
  markitai init                            Create a configuration file
  markitai doctor                          Check models and optional backends

Exit status: 0 success; 1 failure; 2 usage error or provider batch still pending;
10 some batch items failed; 130/143 interrupted.

Inspect or edit configuration

Usage: markitai config [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list      Show the effective configuration; secrets are redacted
  path      Show which configuration file is in use
  validate  Check a configuration file against the schema
  get       Print one value; sections print as JSON
  set       Validate and save one value; invalid values are not written
  edit      Edit settings in a terminal; each value is validated and saved at once

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Configuration:
  -c, --config <PATH>
          Configuration path; must exist except for config set/edit, which can create it
      --config-json <JSON>
          Deep-merge inline JSON over the config file; explicit conversion flags still win

Keys use dot notation, e.g. llm.enabled or llm.model_list[0].model_name. The file in
use is -c, then MARKITAI_CONFIG, then ./markitai.json, then the user config.json.

Examples:
  markitai config list -f table           Show every effective setting
  markitai config get llm.enabled         Read one value
  markitai config set output.dir ./out    Validate and save one value
  markitai config path                    Show which file is in use

Inspect or clear the LLM and URL fetch caches

Usage: markitai cache [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  stats        Show cache entry counts and disk use
  clear        Clear the LLM and URL fetch caches
  spa-domains  Inspect or clear learned browser-domain routing

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Configuration:
  -c, --config <PATH>
          Configuration path; must exist except for config set/edit, which can create it
      --config-json <JSON>
          Deep-merge inline JSON over the config file; explicit conversion flags still win

Examples:
  markitai cache stats                    Entry counts and disk use
  markitai cache stats -v --limit 10      Recent LLM entries per model
  markitai cache clear -y                 Clear without a confirmation prompt
